# Prior to running any code

Please download the data from
<https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/stefanoleone992/mutual-funds-and-etfs>,
and store the file within a data/ folder in the working directory. If
the data is already stored then please skip this step.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(writexl)
source('tools.R')
```

## 1. Load and clean the data

```{r clean-data}
columns <- c(
  "fund_return_ytd",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio",
  "total_net_assets",
  "inception_date",
  "asset_stocks",
  "asset_bonds",
  "annual_holdings_turnover",
  "fund_price_earning_ratio",
  "fund_sector_technology"
)

funds <- rbind(
  transform(read.csv("data/ETFs.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))[columns],
            etf_indicator = 1),
  transform(read.csv("data/MutualFunds.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))[columns],
            etf_indicator = 0)
)

funds <- funds |>
  mutate(
    fund_age_years = as.numeric(as.Date("2021-01-01") - as.Date(inception_date)) / 365.25
  ) |>
  filter(fund_age_years > 0) |>
  mutate(
    pe_reported = as.integer(!is.na(fund_price_earning_ratio)),
    pe_centered_when_reported = {
      pe <- fund_price_earning_ratio
      median_pe <- median(pe, na.rm = TRUE)
      ifelse(is.na(pe), median_pe, pe) - median_pe
    }
  ) |>
  select(-inception_date)

# Use the two P/E terms in the model and keep the raw P/E in funds for the audit.
model_data <- select(funds, -fund_price_earning_ratio)
model_data <- model_data[complete.cases(model_data), ]
```

### Sample and missingness audit

```{r part2-eda-sample, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
local({
  fund_type <- function(indicator) {
    factor(indicator, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"))
  }
  eligible_type <- fund_type(funds$etf_indicator)
  model_type <- fund_type(model_data$etf_indicator)
  sample_counts <- rbind(
    "Eligible before complete-case filtering" = table(eligible_type),
    "Main model sample" = table(model_type),
    "P/E reported in model sample" = table(model_type[model_data$pe_reported == 1L])
  )
  print(knitr::kable(cbind(sample_counts, Total = rowSums(sample_counts))))

  retained <- round(100 * sample_counts[2, ] / sample_counts[1, ], 1)
  print(knitr::kable(rbind("Eligible observations retained (%)" = retained)))

  # Reuse the input columns, with fund age in place of the raw date.
  missing_counts <- sapply(
    split(funds[c(setdiff(columns, "inception_date"), "fund_age_years")], eligible_type),
    function(group) colSums(is.na(group))
  )
  print(knitr::kable(missing_counts))
})
```

## 2. Fit the model

```{r regression}
model <- lm(fund_return_ytd ~ total_net_assets +
    fund_age_years + asset_stocks + asset_bonds +
    annual_holdings_turnover +
    fund_sector_technology + pe_reported + pe_centered_when_reported + 
    fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio * etf_indicator,
  data = model_data
)
```

## 3. Summary tables

```{r}
# Describe fitted model
summary(model)

# Describe cleaned dataset including potentially unused observations
summary(model_data)

# 95% confidence interval
confint(model)

# Test each predictor while accounting for all the others
drop1(model, test = "F")

# ANOVA test
intercept_only <- lm(fund_return_ytd ~ 1, data = model_data)
anova(intercept_only, model)

# The first column is the response; exclude it from predictor covariance
covariance_matrix <- cov(model_data[, -1])
knitr::kable(signif(covariance_matrix, 4))
```

## 4. Plots and model diagnostics

```{r}
plots <- model_plots(model, point_cex = 1.5)

plots$qq()                                 # One plot
plots$show(c("qq", "residuals_vs_fitted"))  # Selected plots
plots$show()
```

```{r}
checks <- check_model(model, plots = FALSE)
head(checks$flagged)
```
